vision_features.image_context: Close-up of a soybean plant showing a green stem with visible fine hairs (pubescence), at least one broad lower leaf, and what appear to be developing or maturing pods. The background shows dry soil, crop residue, and dried/mature pods from surrounding plants. Multiple plant organs are visible: stem, leaf, and pods.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Lower broad leaf — surface-wide distribution of multiple small to medium marks:
   - Location: Scattered across the entire upper leaf surface, concentrated more toward the center and lower half of the leaf
   - Size: Individual marks range from pinpoint (~1mm) to small-medium (~4–7mm diameter)
   - Shape: Mostly circular to slightly irregular, some with slightly angular edges
   - Color of main body: Reddish-brown to tan-brown, dry-looking
   - Border/margin: Many marks are surrounded by a pale yellow-green to yellow halo, creating a lighter ring around the brown center
   - Texture: Appear dry and flat to slightly sunken; some larger marks show tissue that looks papery or collapsed
   - Surface structures: No obvious raised structures; a few of the larger marks appear to have tiny dark specks (~0.5mm) within the brown center tissue
   - Distribution: Scattered uniformly across the leaf surface, with no strong concentration at edges vs. center veins; some coalescence of adjacent marks visible in the lower-central portion of the leaf

2. General leaf color change:
   - The overall leaf background color is uneven — green interspersed with patches of pale yellow-green and yellow, particularly between the vein areas
   - This yellowing is diffuse and interveinal in character, covering roughly 30–40% of the leaf surface

3. One pod visible at upper left:
   - Color: Orange-brown, appearing shriveled or collapsed compared to the more typical tan-colored pods visible in the background
   - Texture: Appears slightly wrinkled/deflated
   - Size: Approximately 25–30mm long, narrow

4. Stem node area (mid-image):
   - A small developing pod bud/structure at the node appears green and healthy; no obvious discoloration noted there
vision_features.absences:
1. No powdery or dusty white coating is visible on any leaf surface or stem.
2. No raised pustule-like bumps or blister structures are visible on the underside of the leaf (underside not directly shown, but the upper surface shows no corresponding raised structures).
3. No visible thread-like fungal growth or slimy exudate on the marks or stem.
4. No wilting or drooping of the stem or upper leaves — the stem and upper foliage appear turgid and upright.
vision_features.summary: The most severely affected organ is the lower broad leaf, which displays numerous small circular to slightly irregular dry brown marks, each typically surrounded by a pale yellow to yellow-green halo, scattered uniformly across the leaf surface. The overall leaf background shows diffuse interveinal yellowing affecting roughly a third of the blade. One pod near the base of the image appears shriveled and orange-brown compared to the dry tan pods in the background. The single most striking visual feature is the combination of the dense population of reddish-brown circular marks with distinct yellow halos distributed across the otherwise still-green leaf, giving it a spotted, mottled appearance.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Septoria brown spot, Bacterial pustule, Downy mildew, Soybean rust, Soybean vein necrosis, Insect and mite Injury
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Phytophthora, Sudden death syndrome, White Mold, Anthracnose, Brown Stem Rot, Charcoal Rot, Herbicide injury, Fungicide injury, Late season frost damage, Lightning damage
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. Diaporthe complex (stem canker), Fusarium root rot and wilt, Pythium seedling blight and root rot, Rhizoctonia seedling blight and root rot, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Charcoal rot, Herbicide injury, Early season frost damage, Insect and mite injury
────────────────────────────────────────
